task_title: 지원 Python/Torch/CuPy/runtime 최소·최대 버전을 실제 설치 시험으로 확정한다

physics_configuration.trials: one fresh venv per trial from the base interpreter (Python 3.10.2) on D:/TorchFDTD/.local/venvs, the wheel of the current tree installed with pip --find-links D:/TorchFDTD/.local/wheels, then (a) the probe script D:/TorchFDTD/.local/tmp/g8/probe_trial.py from a directory outside the checkout: import torchfdtd from the venv prefix, a 2D CPU run (20 x 20 cells, 80 steps), Result.save and Result.load, torch.from_numpy interop; (b) for trials whose probe passes, the CPU subset tests/test_solver.py tests/test_api.py tests/test_torch_interop.py tests/test_project_compatibility.py tests/test_doctor.py run by the venv's pytest entry point (so the checkout is not on sys.path)
trial_matrix: torch 2.2.2+cpu (the oldest torch the old pyproject allowed) with the numpy pip resolves (2.2.6)
torch 2.14.0+cpu (the newest CPU build for Python 3.10 on the day of the run) with numpy 2.2.6: the clean-install record
torch 2.10.0+cu126 with cupy-cuda12x 13.6.0 on CUDA runtime 12.6, driver 591.86, RTX 3060: the clean-install record and the development host
Python 3.12.7 (Anaconda base interpreter) with the newest CPU torch for 3.12, if the download succeeds
Python 3.9 (installed on the host) must be refused by pip through Requires-Python
physics_configuration.doctor: torchfdtd doctor and --json; tests/test_doctor.py monkeypatches torch.cuda.is_available, torch.version.cuda, nvidia-smi parsing, the CuPy probe and the fused-kernel probe to cover: no CUDA torch build, CUDA build without a driver, CUDA build with a driver but no device, driver too old for the torch runtime, CuPy missing, CuPy broken, kernel compile failure; the real fused launch runs on the development host
physics_configuration.not_tried: cupy-cuda12x other than 13.6.0; CUDA runtimes other than 12.6; drivers other than 591.86; torch builds between 2.4.1 and 2.10.0 and between 2.10.0 and 2.14.0; Python 3.11 and 3.13; Linux and macOS

reference_method: actual pip installations and executions; a version is supported only when its probe passed and its CPU subset had no failures; a version is excluded from pyproject.toml when its probe failed

observables.name: probe_status
observables.definition: per trial: import location, run, save/load, torch/numpy interop

observables.name: subset_results
observables.definition: per trial with a passing probe: passed, failed, skipped of the CPU subset

observables.name: doctor_checks
observables.definition: cuda, driver, cupy, fused_kernels, backend entries and the exit code

acceptance_limits.bounds: pyproject.toml lower bounds equal the oldest trial that passed the probe and the subset with the numpy that pip resolves; a numpy constraint is added when the oldest torch needs one; docs/INSTALL.md lists every trial with its outcome and does not claim untried versions
acceptance_limits.doctor: exit 0 and backend cpu/torch in the CPU environment; exit 0, fused_kernels ok and backend cuda/fused in the CUDA environment; every monkeypatched situation in tests/test_doctor.py yields the expected status and message; the real launch on the RTX 3060 reports 20 steps on 400 cells
acceptance_limits.subset: 0 failed, 0 errors in every trial that is claimed supported (CUDA-only tests skip)
acceptance_limits.source_of_limits: COMPLETION_PROGRAM_KO.md G8-06; pass/fail on real installations, no numeric threshold
